Team — quick summary of the first-pass trade study (attached matrix). High-level findings:

- Setup: Dedicated g5.48x (A100-equivalent), single-GPU runs for 13B; pipeline for 70B to approximate latency. All tests run with same seed and prompt batching identical.

- Latency / throughput (relative to FP16 baseline):
  - AWQ-4bit: ~1.9x tokens/sec increase, p95 latency reduced ~28% on 13B; on 70B approx 1.6x tokens/sec, p95 -22%.
  - GPTQ-4bit: ~1.6x tokens/sec increase, p95 latency reduced ~18% on 13B; smaller gains on 70B.
  - FP8 (mixed): ~2.3x tokens/sec on 13B, p95 -35%; on 70B ~2.0x tokens/sec, p95 -30%.

- Quality (delta vs FP16 baseline on critical intents):
  - AWQ-4bit: average intent accuracy drop 0.6% (within tolerance), a few extraction EM drops up to 1.8% on edge cases.
  - GPTQ-4bit: average drop 1.3% with occasional regressions ~2.5% on extraction-heavy prompts.
  - FP8 (mixed): average drop 0.9% but higher variance; some prompts show instability without per-batch calibration (we ran a one-off calibration and saw variability reduce).

- Notes on stability & ops:
  - AWQ seems most stable across our runs and requires no per-batch calibration in our infra.
  - GPTQ shows more sensitivity to model architecture and requires careful ops (per-layer tuning) to avoid outlier regressions.
  - FP8 delivers best perf but may need an ops process (occasional calibration) if you want consistent tail behavior; hardware support is improving but check your on-prem GPU fp8 drivers.

- Recommendation (pilot): For Acme’s constraints (low regression tolerance + desire for good perf) — start with Redwood-2-13B + AWQ-4bit on dedicated pool for pilot. If cost/throughput needs grow, consider FP8-mixed for non-critical routes after additional stability testing. Reserve 70B+ AWQ as a backup for particularly difficult dialogs.

I attached quantization_tradeoff_matrix.xlsx and a short readme. Happy to expand the matrix with per-prompt breakouts if Alex wants to see examples.
